latest_release.body:
<!--

![v2.23.1](https://res.cloudinary.com/dza7lstvk/image/upload/v1795705520/Releases/v2-23-1-5eeb2f.png)

# v2.23.1: Shipping Validation, Auth Callback Hook, S3 Upload Hardening

Cart items linked to a shipping profile now require a shipping method before checkout. This release also adds an authCallbackValidated workflow hook that exposes OAuth provider data for custom post-authentication logic.

CMS_BREAK -->

Docs MCP users can update their project using the following prompt:

```bash
Update my Medusa project to v2.23.1
```

## Highlights

### Shipping Required for Items with Shipping Profiles

**Behavior change**

> Affects stores with product variants linked to a shipping profile. Carts containing such items now require a shipping method before the order can be placed.

Cart completion now validates that a shipping method is provided for all line items whose variants are linked to a shipping profile. If your checkout flow does not collect a shipping method for shippable items, those carts will now fail to complete after upgrading.

[#17936](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/17936)

---

### Auth Callback Hook with Provider Data

The auth callback workflow now has a `authCallbackValidated` hook after a successful OAuth validation. The hook receives the authenticated identity along with the provider's raw authentication data, enabling custom post-authentication logic such as storing OAuth tokens or syncing user attributes from the provider.

A new `storeTokens` option on the callback workflow lets you persist the provider's tokens directly from the hook subscriber.

[#17980](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/17980)

---

### Signed File Size in S3 Presigned Upload URLs

The S3 file provider now signs the file size into presigned upload URLs. S3 rejects any upload whose content length does not match the size signed into the URL, preventing unauthorized oversized uploads.

[#17923](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/17923)

## Features

*   feat(core-flows,auth): add an authCallbackValidated hook with the provider's data, and a storeTokens option by [@srindom](https://github.com/srindom) in [#17980](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/17980)
*   feat(file-s3): sign the file size into presigned upload URLs by [@peterlgh7](https://github.com/peterlgh7) in [#17923](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/17923)

*   fix(core-flows): only restore the reservations deleted by deleteReservationsByLineItemsStep on compensation by [@NicolasGorga](https://github.com/NicolasGorga) in [#18007](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/18007)
*   fix(draft-order): stop capping draft order item quantities at 100 by [@medusa-os-bot](https://github.com/apps/medusa-os-bot) in [#18012](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/pull/18012)

Medusa

Documentation | Website

Building blocks for digital commerce

Medusa is an open-source commerce platform with a built-in framework for customization. Use it to build B2B or DTC stores, marketplaces, distributor platforms, PoS systems, and other applications that need commerce primitives such as products, carts, orders, and payments, without reinventing core commerce logic. ## Getting Started The fastest way to get started is with [Medusa Cloud](https://medusajs.com/cloud/), a managed environment for Medusa applications with automated deployments, scaling, and maintenance. [Get started on Medusa Cloud](https://cloud.medusajs.com). To create a Medusa application locally, you need Node.js v22.22.0 or later and a running PostgreSQL database. Then run: ```bash npx create-medusa-app@latest my-medusa-store ``` This sets up the Medusa server and admin dashboard, and optionally the Next.js Starter Storefront. See the [installation guide](https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/installation) for all options, or [install with Docker](https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/installation/docker). ## Repository structure This is a Yarn workspaces monorepo. Every Medusa package published to npm lives under [`packages`](./packages). | Path | Contents | | --- | --- | | [`packages/medusa`](./packages/medusa) | `@medusajs/medusa`: the main package installed in Medusa applications. Holds the Store and Admin API routes, CLI commands, subscribers, and jobs, and re-exports the modules and `@medusajs/core-flows`. | | [`packages/core/*`](./packages/core) | Core libraries: the framework runtime (`framework`), types, utils, Workflows SDK, Modules SDK, predefined workflows (`core-flows`), Query, orchestration, and the JS SDK. | | [`packages/modules/*`](./packages/modules) | Commerce Modules (product, cart, order, pricing, payment, and more) and Infrastructure Modules (event bus, caching, file, locking, workflow engine, and more). | | [`packages/modules/providers/*`](./packages/modules/providers) | Module Providers, such as Stripe payments, S3 file storage, SendGrid notifications, Redis locking and caching, and auth providers for email/password, GitHub, Google, and OIDC. | | [`packages/admin/*`](./packages/admin) | The Medusa Admin dashboard and the SDK, Vite plugin, and bundler used to build and extend it. | | [`packages/design-system/*`](./packages/design-system) | Medusa UI: the React component library, icons, Tailwind preset, and a Figma import tool. | | [`packages/cli/*`](./packages/cli) | CLI tools: `create-medusa-app`, the `medusa` CLI, OpenAPI tooling, and the HTTP types generator. | | [`packages/plugins/*`](./packages/plugins) | Official plugins, such as draft orders and loyalty. | | [`integration-tests`](./integration-tests) | HTTP and module integration test suites run against a real PostgreSQL database. | | [`www`](./www) | The source of the [Medusa documentation](https://docs.medusajs.com) website. | ## About Medusa Medusa's commerce modules are open-source and freely available on npm. Enterprise Edition features are identified separately in the repository. Learn more about [Medusa's architecture](https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/introduction/architecture) and [Commerce Modules](https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules) in the documentation. ## Upgrades & Integrations Follow the [Release Notes](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/releases) to keep your Medusa project up-to-date. Check out all [available Medusa integrations](https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/integrations). ## Community & Contributions The core team is available in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/discussions), where you can create issues, share ideas, and discuss the roadmap. The [Contribution Guide](./CONTRIBUTING.md) describes how to contribute to the codebase and documentation. Join the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/medusajs) to meet and discuss with other community members. ## Other channels - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/issues) - [Community Discord](https://discord.gg/medusajs) - [Twitter](https://twitter.com/medusajs) - [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/medusajs) - [Medusa Blog](https://medusajs.com/blog/) ## License Medusa uses an open-core model. The core is licensed under the [MIT License](./LICENSE). The Enterprise Edition packages identified in [ENTERPRISE-LICENSE.md](./ENTERPRISE-LICENSE.md) (`@medusajs/rbac`, `@medusajs/auth-oidc`, and `@medusajs/audit`) require a commercial agreement with MedusaJS, Inc.
